> **Pipeline step 05 — effort / catch summary table.**
>
> **Purpose.** Rebuilds the survey × water-year effort and catch table directly from the combined
> tow file (EDSM and TPS, WY2017–2021, December–June).
>
> **Input.** `data/All_Surveys_Combined_v7.3.csv`. **Output.** `output_figs/pub_table_tows_all.csv`.

```{r project-root, include=FALSE}
# Every path in this notebook (data/, fits_*/, output_figs/, cache/) is relative to the
# REPOSITORY ROOT, not to this file's sub-folder. Walk up from the working directory to the
# folder holding the .Rproj file, and make knitr (and RStudio's chunk-by-chunk notebook
# mode) run every chunk from there. Base R only -- no extra package needed.
find_repo_root <- function(path = getwd()) {
  p <- normalizePath(path)
  while (!length(list.files(p, pattern = "\\.Rproj$"))) {
    if (dirname(p) == p) stop("No .Rproj file found above ", path)
    p <- dirname(p)
  }
  p
}
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = find_repo_root())
```
Reproduces `output_figs/pub_table_tows_all.csv` (survey x water-year effort/catch
summary) directly from `data/All_Surveys_Combined_v7.3.csv`.

Scope: EDSM and TPS only, water years 2017-2021, months December-June (the
Dec-Jun parr-migration window used throughout the analysis -- this is what makes
the EDSM tow counts match the published table).

```{r setup, message=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
```

Load data. The file has a UTF-8 BOM, so the first column name comes in as
`ï..Survey` / `﻿Survey` depending on the reader; fix it explicitly.

```{r load}
all_surveys <- read.csv("data/All_Surveys_Combined_v7.3.csv",
                        stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
names(all_surveys)[1] <- "Survey"

dim(all_surveys)
```

Filter to the surveys, water years, and months of interest.

```{r filter}
migration_months <- c(12, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6)

tows <- all_surveys %>%
  filter(Survey %in% c("EDSM", "TPS"),
         Water_Year >= 2017, Water_Year <= 2021,
         Month %in% migration_months) %>%
  # n_l_75 is NA when no fish were measured; those tows caught no <75 mm fish
  mutate(n_l_75 = replace_na(n_l_75, 0))

tows %>% count(Survey, Water_Year)
```

Summarise. CPUE is pooled over the whole water year -- sum of catch divided by
sum of volume -- and scaled by 10,000 (fish per 10,000 m^3), which is the scale
used in the published table. Detections are tows with nonzero
`Chinook_Salmon_Catch` **or** nonzero `n_l_75`.

For TPS there is one row per StationCode, so Sites == Tows. For EDSM each site
was towed several times, so Sites counts distinct StationCodes and Tows counts
rows.

```{r summarise}
cpue_scale <- 10000

# One place that defines every metric, so single-year rows and multi-year
# rollups are guaranteed to be computed identically. CPUE is always
# sum(catch) / sum(Volume) over whatever rows are passed in -- never an
# average of per-year CPUEs.
summarise_tows <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    summarise(
      Sites               = n_distinct(StationCode),
      Tows                = n(),
      Detections          = sum(Chinook_Salmon_Catch > 0 | n_l_75 > 0),
      `Total Catch`       = sum(Chinook_Salmon_Catch),
      CPUE                = sum(Chinook_Salmon_Catch) / sum(Volume) * cpue_scale,
      `Detections < 75mm` = sum(n_l_75 > 0),
      `Catch < 75mm`      = sum(n_l_75),
      `CPUE < 75mm`       = sum(n_l_75) / sum(Volume) * cpue_scale,
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}

by_year <- tows %>%
  group_by(Survey, Water_Year) %>%
  summarise_tows() %>%
  transmute(Survey, water_year = as.character(Water_Year),
            row_type = "year", across(Sites:`CPUE < 75mm`))

by_year
```

### Multi-year rollup rows

Pooled across the years in each range: catch and Volume are summed over all
tows in the range *first*, then divided -- so these CPUEs are volume-weighted
totals, not averages of the yearly CPUEs shown above.

Edit `rollup_spec` to change which ranges get a row.

```{r rollups}
# TPS ran 2018-2021; EDSM ran 2017-2021. First two rows cover the years the two
# surveys overlap (2018-2021) so they are directly comparable; the third adds
# EDSM's extra 2017 season for its full-span total.
rollup_spec <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Survey, ~year_from, ~year_to,
  "TPS",         2018,     2021,
  "EDSM",        2018,     2021,
  "EDSM",        2017,     2021
)

rollups <- rollup_spec %>%
  purrr::pmap_dfr(function(Survey, year_from, year_to) {
    tows %>%
      filter(Survey == !!Survey,
             Water_Year >= year_from, Water_Year <= year_to) %>%
      summarise_tows() %>%
      transmute(Survey = !!Survey,
                water_year = paste0(year_from, "-", year_to),
                row_type = "multi-year", across(Sites:`CPUE < 75mm`))
  })

rollups
```

Sanity check: the count columns in a rollup should equal the sum of the
per-year rows it covers, while CPUE should *not* equal the mean of the yearly
CPUEs (it is volume-weighted).

```{r rollup-check}
purrr::pmap_dfr(rollup_spec, function(Survey, year_from, year_to) {
  yrs <- by_year %>%
    filter(Survey == !!Survey, water_year %in% as.character(year_from:year_to))
  rol <- rollups %>%
    filter(Survey == !!Survey, water_year == paste0(year_from, "-", year_to))
  tibble::tibble(
    Survey = Survey, range = paste0(year_from, "-", year_to),
    tows_match   = sum(yrs$Tows)  == rol$Tows,
    sites_match  = sum(yrs$Sites) == rol$Sites,
    catch_match  = sum(yrs$`Total Catch`) == rol$`Total Catch`,
    det_match    = sum(yrs$Detections) == rol$Detections,
    pooled_CPUE  = rol$CPUE,
    mean_of_yrly = mean(yrs$CPUE)
  )
})
```

Combine, placing each survey's rollup rows directly beneath its yearly rows.

```{r combine}
pub_table <- bind_rows(by_year, rollups) %>%
  arrange(factor(Survey, levels = c("TPS", "EDSM")),
          factor(row_type, levels = c("year", "multi-year")),
          water_year)

pub_table
```

Compare against the original file.

```{r compare}
orig <- read.csv("output_figs/pub_table_tows_all.csv", check.names = FALSE)

check <- orig %>%
  rename_with(~ paste0(.x, "_orig"), -c(Survey, water_year)) %>%
  mutate(water_year = as.character(water_year)) %>%
  left_join(filter(pub_table, row_type == "year"), by = c("Survey", "water_year"))

# absolute difference in every numeric column
check %>%
  transmute(Survey, water_year,
            d_Sites      = Sites      - Sites_orig,
            d_Tows       = Tows       - Tows_orig,
            d_Det        = Detections - Detections_orig,
            d_Catch      = `Total Catch` - `Total Catch_orig`,
            d_CPUE       = CPUE       - CPUE_orig,
            d_Det75      = `Detections < 75mm` - `Detections < 75mm_orig`,
            d_Catch75    = `Catch < 75mm` - `Catch < 75mm_orig`,
            d_CPUE75     = `CPUE < 75mm` - `CPUE < 75mm_orig`)
```

Everything reproduces exactly except EDSM site counts in WY2017 (123 here vs 124
published) and WY2018 (194 here vs 193 published). Tow counts, catch, detections
and all CPUE values match to full printed precision in every year, and no
alternative site definition tried (lat/long pairs, StationCode x Region,
StationCode x lat/long) changes those two numbers -- so this looks like drift
between the data version used for the original table and v7.3, not a difference
in how sites are counted.

## Units check: is `Volume` in m^3 or ft^3?

Worth confirming, since CPUE is reported per 10,000 volume units. Nothing in the
project converts tow `Volume` between cfs/cms -- every `0.0283168` in the repo
applies to `OUT` / `OUT_Moving_Mean_30d` (Dayflow Delta outflow), never to
`Volume`. EDSM volumes are cubic meters per the EDI metadata (edi.415).

For TPS, back-calculate the net mouth area from the raw survey file: tow volume
divided by flowmeter distance should recover a constant per net type, and that
constant is diagnostic of the units.

```{r units-check}
tps_raw <- read.csv("data/tps_bug_allspp_data.csv") %>%
  distinct(site_id, .keep_all = TRUE)

tps_raw %>%
  mutate(mouth_area = fish_tow_volume / flowmeter_distance) %>%
  group_by(fish_net) %>%
  summarise(n = sum(!is.na(mouth_area)),
            area_if_m2  = round(median(mouth_area, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
            # what the same number would mean if volume were ft^3 (1 ft^2 = 0.092903 m^2)
            area_if_ft2 = round(median(mouth_area, na.rm = TRUE) * 0.092903, 3),
            .groups = "drop")
```

The ratio is an exact constant within each net type: Kodiak 16.72, Otter 6.541,
Mamou 6.057, Tenera 4.459.

The Otter row settles it. The CDFW Bay Study otter trawl has a documented mouth
opening of 1.5 m x 4.3 m = **6.45 m^2**, and the back-calculated constant is
6.541 -- a 1.4% match against a rounded published spec. If `Volume` were cubic
feet the same constant would imply a 0.61 m^2 mouth, an order of magnitude too
small. TPS `Volume` is therefore in **cubic meters**, same as EDSM.

Consistent with this, TPS and EDSM Kodiak tows are the same order of magnitude
(median 7,750 vs 4,002 m^3); a ft^3/m^3 mixup would put them ~35x apart.

**Conclusion: no unit conversion is needed.** Both surveys report `Volume` in
m^3, and CPUE in the table is fish per 10,000 m^3.

Write out under a new name so the original is preserved.

```{r write}
out_path <- "output_figs/pub_table_tows_all_v7.3_rebuild.csv"
write.csv(pub_table, out_path, row.names = FALSE)
out_path
```
